text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to financially assist the national telephone company Rom Telecom RA in its further growth and restructuring.
- Romanian company Rocar SA won a tender to supply 300 buses to the Bucharest public transport authority RATB.
ADEVARUL
- Labour Minister Alexandru Athanasiu said wage taxes were expected to drop by up to 8.0 percent, with wages of up to 200,000 lei monthly being tax free.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Several commercial banks have raised their interest rates following central bank moves to tighten its monetary policy.

- A new unit trust -- Danube Fund -- has started operating in Romania. It is a venture capital fund which plans to invest in companies which already turned private or are about to go into private hands.
LIBERTATEA
- Foreign investors complain primitive accounting systems, cvorruption and banking commissions are brakes to investment in Romania.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Romania and the International Monetary Fund, now discussing new loan arrangements, tackled the 1997 state budget, apparently agreeing that the deficit might account for up to 10 percent of the gross domestic product.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's court of accounts (CC) checked more than 600 formerly state-owned companies and found out that 87 percent of them were illegally privatised, CC president Ioan Bogdan quoted as saying.
- Greece supports Romania's bid to join NATO and the EU, Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos told his Romanian counterpart Adrian Severin.
ADEVARUL
- Police in the Black Sea Port of Constanta found 1,000 kilo of hashish allegedly smuggled from South Africa.
- Police is investigating state-owned oil trading company Petrolimportexport on suspicions of alleged fraud worth $50 million by company top officials.
- Police arrested three suspects allegedly involved in ethnic clashes between Romanians and Gypsies in the village of Hadareni, in 1993. Four people died in the violence.
- Lower Chamber of Deputies's commission for foreign policy called ambassadors to NATO member-countries to gather in Bucharest for talks on a common strategy to win early admission into the alliance.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- A poor family with two children will get a monthly allowance of 90,000 lei, Labour and Social Protection Minister Alexandru Athanasiu said.

- The former ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) will file a complaint with the Council of Europe against alledged "political cleansing" by the new government in local administration, newspaper says.
- Newly appointed army Chief of Staff Constantin Degeratu said the country's integration in NATO was top priority.
ZIUA
- Police started inquiries into procedures of awarding of two lucrative GSM licences worth $500 million each to consortia MobilRom and Mobifon. ($= 5,612 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
